title: Definitions shared by every task-repo kind (docs/task-repos.md)

refString.description: A reference, which names its target by path (docs/task-repos.md §2.1, §4): a relative or /-rooted path, <git URL>//<path>, or <alias>:<path>; then optional @<gitref> and #<anchor>

ref.description: An edge that records more than its target: the reference in `ref`, plus the edge's own fields (§4)

principal.description: Who: silo, silo:trigger, grain:<node>, user:<email>, agent:grain:<node>/<run path>, team:<name>#member|approver|admin|maintainer, authenticated

aka.description: Earlier identities from before migration (grain:<deployment>/task/<n>, a settings id, a hub task id): indexed for search, never used to resolve (§2.1)

cadence.description: The cadence keys grain's declarations use (docs/declarations.md); exactly one of them

pinnedRef.description: A reference plus the commit it was read at, so it still resolves after the target is gone (§4)

movedFrom.description: The object's earlier addresses, oldest first; each is now a kind: moved tombstone (§2.1)

rank.description: LexoRank-style key over 0-9a-z, compared bytewise, never ending in 0 (§5.2)

contextEntry.description: One thing a run's sandbox holds (docs/task-repos.md §5.6): a repo, a repo folder (a path ending in /), or a file (an object or an asset), by reference; or, with mode: use, a capability the run requests (§5.7). A bare string is {ref: <string>, mode: read}, so a bare string never requests a capability

input.description: Templates only, in place of ref: a declared input of type ref (or a list of ref)

mode.description: write: push the run's own branch, based on the entry's @<branch>; only for a repo or a repo folder. use: request the kind: capability object the ref names; nothing of the file itself lands, only what the capability materialises (§5.7)

path.description: Where it lands, relative to the sandbox's working root; default: work/<repo name>/ for repos and folders, context/<host>/<repo path>/<path> for files

depth.description: Files only: also materialise what the Markdown body links to, this many links deep, under the caps

reducers.description: use only: reducers of the task's own, applied after the capability's chain. They can only narrow it further
